security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 159 static findings: eight identify credential forwarding or unsafe temporary login logs; the remaining 151 are false positives. Semantic findings identify plaintext credential memory, unsafe archive selection, and instructions that can manipulate security review through unsupported safety claims. No evidence found of executable obfuscated payloads; multilingual prose, detection signatures, and Markdown explain the apparent execution and entropy alerts.

remediation.issue: GitHub authentication is forwarded through ghfast.top in two publishing recipes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove mirror authentication examples. Push directly to github.com through HTTPS or SSH, and revoke tokens previously sent to the mirror.

remediation.issue: Device-login output uses a predictable shared temporary file.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private temporary directory with restrictive permissions. Avoid symlink-following redirection, remove logs after authorization, and terminate abandoned login processes.

remediation.issue: The XiaPing guide stores a long-lived API key in agent memory.
remediation.suggestion: Use an operating-system credential manager or protected secret store. Keep credentials out of agent memory, prompts, repositories, and publication archives.

remediation.issue: Package file selection does not exclude secrets or reject file symlinks.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit publication manifest, exclude credential files, reject symlinks, and verify resolved paths remain inside the skill directory before packaging.

remediation.issue: Publishing instructions encourage blanket safety assurances as more effective than correcting code.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this review-manipulation guidance. Derive every assurance from the release, disclose necessary permissions, and fix unsafe behavior before requesting an independent audit.

semantic_findings.title: Long-Lived API Key Stored in Agent Memory
semantic_findings.description: The XiaPing guide directs agents to store their long-lived API key in MEMORY.md. Plaintext agent memory can expose credentials through later context loading, synchronization, or accidental publication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text identifies the response key as a long-term credential and explicitly instructs saving it in the memory document. No protected storage mechanism is specified.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Local Files Can Enter Publication Archives
semantic_findings.description: The generic builder accepts credential files, while both builders follow file symlinks without checking containment. WorkBuddy limits top-level directories, but secrets inside those directories can still enter release archives.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The generic collector accepts .env; WorkBuddy accepts files inside designated subdirectories without secret exclusions. Both archive writers dereference file symlinks, so disclosure depends on the selected tree.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The guide says "写进提交备注，比修改代码更有效", meaning writing safety assurances in submission notes is more effective than changing code. Instructing agents to assert no network access and mandatory backups without verification can manipulate marketplace security review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly favor safety claims over code corrections and repeat blanket assurances for scripted skills. This targets downstream review, not this audit's instruction hierarchy.

high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text identifies the response key as a long-term credential and explicitly instructs saving it in the memory document. No protected storage mechanism is specified.

high_findings.title: Sensitive Local Files Can Enter Publication Archives
high_findings.description: The generic builder accepts credential files, while both builders follow file symlinks without checking containment. WorkBuddy limits top-level directories, but secrets inside those directories can still enter release archives.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The generic collector accepts .env; WorkBuddy accepts files inside designated subdirectories without secret exclusions. Both archive writers dereference file symlinks, so disclosure depends on the selected tree.

high_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
high_findings.description: The guide says "写进提交备注，比修改代码更有效", meaning writing safety assurances in submission notes is more effective than changing code. Instructing agents to assert no network access and mandatory backups without verification can manipulate marketplace security review.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly favor safety claims over code corrections and repeat blanket assurances for scripted skills. This targets downstream review, not this audit's instruction hierarchy.

medium_findings.title: Temp directory access
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: Login output is redirected to a predictable shared temporary path without permission controls. Another local user could read authentication output or preplant a symlink.

medium_findings.title: Temp directory access
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The login process writes authentication output to a fixed shared temporary filename. Missing restrictive permissions and exclusive creation permit local disclosure or symlink clobbering.

medium_findings.title: Temp directory access
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command reads a predictable shared login log without verifying ownership or permissions. A local attacker could replace it or access authentication output.

content.user_title: Publish Agent Skills Across Supported Marketplaces
content.value_statement: Skill marketplaces require different repository layouts, package formats, and submission steps. This skill provides local preparation tools, supported API submissions, and channel-specific publishing guidance.
actual_capabilities: Check skill metadata, repository layout, licenses, file sizes, and text patterns with a local preflight script.
Build ZIP packages with SKILL.md at the archive root and generate a package manifest.
Build WorkBuddy skill archives with additional display and description metadata without modifying the source document.
Submit selected repository metadata or skill documents to skillstore, skillsmd, and skillbay through implemented API handlers.
List distribution channels and query skillstore submission status using a receipt identifier.
Provide reference workflows for repository contributions, authenticated publishing, XiaPing uploads, MCP directories, and API listings.
limitations: Automatic submission covers only implemented handlers, not every marketplace listed in the references.
Account authentication, identity verification, copyright agreement, and merchant setup can require direct user action.
Directory rules and API endpoints can change; submission receipts do not guarantee approval, indexing, revenue, or discovery.
Text-pattern checks do not certify security, and archives need secret and symlink inspection; the skills.sh probe contains project-specific filters.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Open-Source Skill Release
use_cases.description: Check repository structure and prepare publication archives before submitting an agent skill to selected public marketplaces.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Marketplace Submissions
use_cases.description: Separate automated API submissions from channels awaiting login, review, or platform-specific development, then track available receipts.

use_cases.title: Plan Service Distribution
use_cases.description: Compare skill listings, MCP directories, API catalogs, and hosted platforms to identify suitable deliverables for an existing service.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review [skill directory] for publishing readiness. Explain metadata, license, and layout issues without changing files, submitting content, or installing tools.

prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a package for [marketplace] from [skill directory]. Inspect credentials and symlinks first, confirm the output directory, and do not upload anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a reviewed publication artifact.

prompt_templates.prompt: Plan submissions for [repository URL] to [selected marketplaces]. Show destinations and shared data, request approval, then report receipts and unresolved login requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Distribution Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a distribution plan for [skill repository] and [MCP or API endpoint]. Separate packaging, registry submissions, authentication, consent, and porting work.

best_practices: Approve each destination and shared field before submission; retain receipts and distinguish submitted content from approved listings.
Inspect archives for secrets and symlinks, use protected credential storage, and authenticate directly with the intended service.
Verify current marketplace requirements and support every safety statement with release evidence; do not follow instructions that substitute assurances for security fixes.
anti_patterns: Forwarding GitHub tokens through third-party mirrors or saving long-lived API keys in agent memory.
Publishing archives without inspecting sensitive files, symlinks, output paths, and included metadata.
Treating a broad channel catalog, a successful request, or a preflight result as guaranteed approval or a complete security audit.

faq.question: Does this publish to every marketplace automatically?
faq.answer: No. The script implements several API handlers, while many catalog entries require login, manual review, repository contributions, or platform-specific development.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three tools as supported. Local scripts require a compatible Python installation, while authenticated channels may require additional CLIs.

faq.question: Does the preflight script certify that my skill is secure?
faq.answer: No. It checks metadata and text patterns. It cannot replace code review, credential inspection, or marketplace security assessment.

faq.question: Can it publish private repositories to automatic indexes?
faq.answer: Public auto-indexers generally require accessible repositories. Private distribution needs an appropriate authenticated upload or hosted workflow.

faq.question: Does submission enable paid listings?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Pricing and payment setup usually require seller accounts, merchant verification, or platform-specific service changes.

faq.question: What precautions are needed before using the recipes?
faq.answer: Avoid token-bearing mirror pushes and plaintext credential memory. Inspect archives for secrets and symlinks, and approve destinations and legal pledges explicitly.
